description:
CONFIRMED against a reference implementation, not by argument. I built llama.cpp from the vendored clone (crates/kopitiam-ai/vendor/llama.cpp, MSVC/cmake, targets llama-completion + llama-tokenize) and ran it on the SAME .gguf with the SAME prompts, greedy (--temp 0).

THE PROOF, identical 33-token ChatML prompt:
  llama.cpp : 'hello, how can I assist you today?' [end of text]
  kopitiam  : 'I''m a bot, I''m a bot, I''m a chatbot, ...'

Our distribution at that position is FLAT and disagrees hard:
  #0 'I'=12.238  #1 'The'=12.150  #2 'A'=12.007 ... #9 'Hello'=11.237
  llama.cpp's greedy pick 'hello' is our RANK 69, logit 8.771, gap 3.47.
Top-10 spans only 1.0 logit. Not a near-tie flip — a real disagreement.

IT SCALES WITH PROMPT LENGTH (this is the key signature):
  5 tok  'The capital of France is'      -> ours ' Paris'=20.337 rank 0, MATCHES llama.cpp exactly
  8 tok  '...over the lazy'              -> ours ' dog'=22.597 rank 0, MATCHES exactly
  3 tok  'The capital of'                -> llama.cpp ' France'; ours ranks it #2, gap 0.53 (near-tie)
  18 tok 'Once upon a time...near the'   -> ours ' sea. She had'  vs ref ' sea. She loved'
  33 tok plain text ending 'France is'   -> ours ' a.\n\nThe '     vs ref ' Paris. The capital of the'
Confident short prompts agree EXACTLY. Divergence grows with length.

ELIMINATED, each with evidence (do not re-check these):
  Tokenisation: our ids are byte-identical to llama-tokenize for the chat prompt, including the 'ass'+'istant' split. No BOS on either side (add_bos_token=false, honoured).
  Config: every field matches the file for both models (360M theta 100000, 1.7B theta 130000, head_dim/heads/kv/ffn/layers/eps).
  RoPE: split-half/NEOX; tables verified numerically vs hand computation at positions 0,1,5,12,19,33,100 with real params -> max abs diff 0e0.
  Tensor ops vs hand loops at REAL shapes: q@K^T [15,19,19,64] and [15,1,33,64]; probs@V incl. [32,33,33,64]; softmax normalisation; masked softmax; scalar rank-0 div; rms_norm with a NON-UNIFORM weight; silu; gather_rows; causal-mask BROADCAST across all 15 heads. All exact.
  KV cache: concat on dim 1 correct; batched prefill and one-token-at-a-time agree.
  Quantisation vs ggml-quants.c: dequant_q4_k == dequantize_row_q4_K, get_scale_min_k4 matches incl. the q[j-0] case, dequant_q6_k matches incl. the SIGNED i8 scales.
  NOT the quantized kernel: running the whole model with KOPITIAM_FORCE_F32_WEIGHTS=1 (new debug knob, see bridge.rs) gives byte-identical outputs to the quantized path. So the fused kernel is not the cause.
  NOT GQA: the 1.7B is 32/32 (no GQA) and fails the same way.
  MLP is silu(gate)*up -> down; block is pre-norm with correct residuals. Both match llama.cpp's build_llama.

WHAT IT IS NOT: model weakness. The 1.7B fails identically, and llama.cpp gets the right answer from the same file.

NEXT STEP (do this, do not guess): bisect the forward pass numerically against llama.cpp layer by layer. Build its eval-callback example (GGML_DEBUG / examples/eval-callback) which dumps every intermediate tensor, run the same 33-token prompt through both, and compare after each block — embeddings, then attn_norm out, attn out, residual, ffn_norm out, mlp out. The first layer whose output diverges localises it. Everything cheaper than that has been tried and is listed above.

Repro:
  printf 'hello\n' | kopitiam ai chat
  llama.cpp: build/bin/Release/llama-completion.exe -m <gguf> -e -p '<|im_start|>system\n...<|im_start|>assistant\n' -n 20 --temp 0 -no-cnv

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
FIXED in commit 406cd3ed44. Root cause: WRONG RoPE PAIRING CONVENTION for llama-architecture models.

rope.rs implemented split-half (NEOX) exclusively and its docs asserted 'LLaMA and every model derived from it - including every Qwen release - uses split-half'. Only the Qwen half is true. Per llama.cpp's llama_model_rope_type (src/llama-model.cpp, switch commented 'use what we call a normal RoPE, operating on pairs of consecutive head values'), LLM_ARCH_LLAMA is NORM/interleaved and LLM_ARCH_QWEN2 is NEOX/split-half. SmolLM2 reports general.architecture=llama, so DEFAULT_MODEL_ID ran with mispositioned Q and K.

The trap underneath the trap: HuggingFace LlamaAttention really does use rotate_half (split-half) in Python, but convert_hf_to_gguf.py PERMUTES the Q/K rows so ggml's interleaved rotation reproduces it. Reading the HF modelling code and concluding split-half is right about the architecture and wrong about the file.

Why it hid: at position 0 the angle is 0 so both conventions are the identity; error grows with position. Short prompts stayed correct ('The capital of France is' -> ' Paris', '...over the lazy' -> ' dog') while long ones degraded, which reads as 'small weak model'. It is also invisible to shape/sanity checks since both conventions preserve each pair's norm. Both facts are now regression tests.

Found by layer-by-layer bisection against llama.cpp's eval-callback, which is what finally worked after every component had been individually verified correct in isolation:
                ours(before)   ours(after)   llama.cpp
  inp_embd        -6.247214     -6.247214    -6.247214
  attn_norm-0     -4.775917     -4.775917    -4.775916
  Qcur-0.rope    -32.685047    -37.304260   -37.306450   <- divergence starts here
  Kcur-0.rope    +59.619232    +59.988953   +59.997219
  attn_out-0     +11.727785    +11.524756   +11.535707
  blk.0.out         -236.6        -241.21      -242.45

Fix: RopeKind::{Interleaved,SplitHalf} selected per architecture by config::rope_kind_for_architecture, mirroring llama.cpp's table; element indexing transcribed from ggml's rotate_pairs. Unknown architectures keep the split-half default, documented as a guess.

A TEST WAS ASSERTING THE BUG: llama_and_qwen2_arch_with_identical_weights_produce_bit_identical_logits demanded the two architectures agree bit-for-bit because 'nothing in the forward pass branches on the arch string'. That premise WAS the bug, and the test passed for exactly as long as the bug existed. Rewritten to assert the opposite, with the reasoning recorded.

Verified: ai chat 'hello' -> 'i'm happy to assist you. what can i help you with today?'; 'What is the capital of France?' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.' 142 runtime tests green, netfetch canonical gate green, clippy -D warnings clean.

Knock-on: bd-2c2 (wgpu offload) is unblocked - the CPU forward pass now agrees with llama.cpp, so a GPU/CPU/llama.cpp three-way comparison is finally meaningful.

title: runtime: our forward pass diverges from llama.cpp, and the gap GROWS with prompt length
